# PROJ concerns

<!-- generated by report/proj_concerns.py from suites/projections/proj-concerns.json and summary.json; do not edit -->

Concerns about PROJ itself, as opposed to the ports, found by the benchmark. Signals are computed against PROJ 9.10.0 (git 5fa31c29) on every run; whether a signal is a real problem is decided by a person and recorded in [proj-concerns.json](../../suites/projections/proj-concerns.json).

**Nothing here has been sent to PROJ unless the entry links to a PROJ issue, pull request or commit.**

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| suspected | flagged, not yet looked at closely |
| confirmed | reproduced with a minimal case outside the benchmark |
| drafted | a fix and a test exist; not filed |
| reported | filed with PROJ by a person (link given) |
| fixed | fixed in PROJ (commit given) |
| not-a-bug | looked at; PROJ is right or the difference is by design |

## Details

### omerc: gamma-only definitions become alpha = 0 through pyproj's Proj()/CRS route

<a id="omerc-gamma-crs-route"></a>Status: **suspected**. Found 2026-10-20. PROJ: not sent to PROJ.

A `+proj=omerc` string with `+gamma` and no `+alpha` comes back from `pyproj.Proj()` or `CRS()` with `+alpha=0` added, which changes the projection. `Transformer.from_pipeline` keeps the string as given, which is why the benchmark uses it. Not yet narrowed down to pyproj or to PROJ's CRS layer.

### eqearth: PROJ's round trip at the poles is 6.6e-6 deg off

<a id="eqearth-pole-roundtrip"></a>Status: **suspected**. Found 2026-10-21. PROJ: not sent to PROJ.

Forward then inverse of lat -90 returns lat -89.9999934. Cause not yet traced: the inverse's Newton tolerance is 1e-11, so the loss is elsewhere, perhaps the clamp of y to MAX_Y or the authalic latitude conversion near the pole. Small, but larger than any other round trip in the suite.

This run: roundtrip on eqearth: worst 6.6e-06 deg at [-180, -90].

### World projections: inverse refuses points exactly on lon +-180 or at a pole

<a id="edge-of-world-inverse"></a>Status: **suspected**. Found 2026-10-22. PROJ: not sent to PROJ.

Every inverse failure in these is on the outline of the map: lon +-180, or a pole that the projection draws as a point or a line. One step inside (lon 179.9999999 for wag4) inverts correctly. Most likely deliberate range checks that reject the boundary itself; still to check whether that is intended.

This run: roundtrip on moll: 8 inverse failures; roundtrip on wag4: 10 inverse failures, worst 8.5e-07 deg at [-180, -90]; roundtrip on wag5: 14 inverse failures; roundtrip on robin: 4 inverse failures; roundtrip on hammer: 36 inverse failures; roundtrip on igh: 15 inverse failures.

### moll: forward x at the poles is 112.5 m, not 0

<a id="moll-pole-newton"></a>Status: **confirmed**. Found 2026-10-21. PROJ: not sent to PROJ.

At lon -180 lat -90, PROJ gives x = -112.5 m where the exact answer is 0 (every meridian meets at the pole). proj4rs, wbprojection, proj4js and math.gl all give 0. In `moll_s_forward()` the Newton step for the auxiliary angle divides by 1 + cos(theta), which goes to 0 at the pole, so convergence there is slow; the loop exits on its step-size test with theta still short of pi/2, and cos(theta) is not quite 0.

This run: consensus on moll: proj4rs, wbprojection, proj4js agree with each other and differ from PROJ by up to 112.5 m forward, 3.6e-15 deg inverse.

### ortho: ellipsoidal inverse returns inf at and next to a visible pole

<a id="ortho-ellipsoidal-pole-inverse"></a>Status: **confirmed**. Found 2026-10-22. PROJ: not sent to PROJ.

With `+proj=ortho +ellps=WGS84 +lat_0=-42 +lon_0=147` the south pole is on the visible side. Forward gives (0, -4745251.365); the inverse of that returns (inf, inf), as it does for lat -89.9999999. At lat -89.99 the round trip is fine, and the spherical case (`+R=6371000`) inverts the pole. Cause not yet traced; the oblique branch of `ortho_e_inverse()` near the pole is the first place to look. Separate from the k_0 entry: with k_0 = 1 and no alpha that patch does not change the seed.

This run: roundtrip on ortho: 11 inverse failures.

### ortho: ellipsoidal oblique inverse fails or lands wrong with k_0 != 1 or alpha != 0

<a id="ortho-oblique-inverse-k0"></a>Status: **drafted**. Found 2026-10-17. PROJ: not sent to PROJ.

`ortho_e_inverse()` unrotates by alpha and divides by k_0, then seeds Newton with `ortho_s_inverse()`, which does both again. With k_0 = 0.9 about 44% of inverses fail; with alpha the seed can converge to the wrong point. A patch and a gie test exist (they move the unrotate and scale out of the spherical inverse into a wrapper). Not in this suite, which uses k_0 = 1 and no alpha.

### eqc: PROJ is ellipsoidal since 2026-01, the ports are spherical

<a id="eqc-ellipsoidal"></a>Status: **not-a-bug**. Found 2026-10-21. PROJ: [6a529ad4](https://github.com/OSGeo/PROJ/commit/6a529ad433d87742ba7163e94fa2fdf043432db1).

PROJ added the ellipsoidal Equidistant Cylindrical method (EPSG 1028) in 6a529ad4; the ports still use the spherical formulas, so they agree with each other and differ from PROJ by 29 km. PROJ is right; this is a porting gap.

This run: consensus on eqc: proj4rs, proj-core, wbprojection agree with each other and differ from PROJ by up to 2.9e+04 m forward, 0.24 deg inverse.

### ortho: three ports agree with each other and differ from PROJ by 33.7 km

<a id="ortho-spherical-ports"></a>Status: **not-a-bug**. Found 2026-10-21. PROJ: nothing to send.

wbprojection, proj4js and math.gl compute ortho on a sphere of radius a. PROJ has used ellipsoidal formulas since 7.2. PROJ is right.

This run: consensus on ortho: wbprojection, proj4js agree with each other and differ from PROJ by up to 3.369e+04 m forward, 3.7 deg inverse.
